'''Nemanja Nedović''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Немања Недовић}}; {{IPA|sh|němaɲa nêːdoʋitɕ|pron}}; born 16 June 1991) is a Serbian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS), the [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He also represented the senior [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbian national basketball team]] internationally. Standing at {{height|m=1.92}}, he can play both the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions.

==Professional career==
===Early years===
Nedović began to train in Italy with Ascoli basketball when he was 11 years of age. He lived there because his father was playing professional [[Team handball|handball]] locally with the Ascoli Piceno Handball. After that, he trained for two years in [[Nova Varoš]]. In 2005, he moved to [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] at the age of 15. He had success in the junior competition, as in 2008 when he became champion with the [[KK Crvena zvezda (youth)|junior team of Crvena zvezda]].

After that, he moved to the first team where he finally made a breakthrough professionally.<ref>{{cite web |title=POVERENJE U MLADI TIM |url=http://www.kkcrvenazvezda.rs/index.php/article/poverenje-u-mladi-tim |work=kkcrvenazvezda.rs |access-date=20 October 2013 |language=sr}}</ref> In his first season with the team, he was scoring in double digits, forcing the team management to extend a contract with him for one more season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Crvena Zvezda keeps Nemanja Nedovic and Uros Nikolic |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/cups/adriatic-league/30910/crvena-zvezda-keeps-nemanja-nedovic-and-uros-nikolic.html |work=Sportando |access-date=20 October 2013}}</ref> He stayed in the club until June 2012.

===Lietuvos rytas===
In the summer of 2012, he signed a contract with the Lithuanian team [[BC Lietuvos rytas|Lietuvos rytas Vilnius]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lietuvos Rytas inks Nedovic |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/98378/180/lietuvos-rytas-inks-nedovic |work=Euroleague |access-date=4 August 2012}}</ref> In his first [[2012–13 Euroleague|EuroLeague]] season with Rytas he averaged 9.8 points, 2.5 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game.

===Golden State Warriors===
On 27 June 2013, Nedović was selected with the 30th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He was later traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] on draft night. He is also the last draft pick called by [[David Stern]] in his career as a [[commissioner of the NBA]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thompson II |first1=Marcus |title=Golden State Warriors get guard Nemanja Nedovic with 30th pick in draft |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/ci_23556932/golden-state-warriors-get-guard-nemanja-nedovic-30th |access-date=10 June 2015 |work=mercurynews.com |date=27 June 2013}}</ref> On 9 July 2013 he signed with the Warriors.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/golden-state-warriors-sign-nemanja-nedovic-contract Golden State Warriors Sign Nemanja Nedovic to Contract]</ref> During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html |title=2013-14 NBA Assignments |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=25 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703151241/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html |archive-date=3 July 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In July 2014, Nedović joined the Warriors for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]] where he averaged 9.4 points, 2.0 rebounds and 2.2 assists in five games.<ref>{{cite web |title=2014 Summer League Player Profile: Nemanja Nedovic |url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2014/players/sl_nemanja_nedovic/index.html |work=NBA.com |access-date=19 July 2014}}</ref> On 11 November 2014, he was waived by the Warriors.<ref>{{cite news |title=Warriors Waive Nemanja Nedovic |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/nedovic-waived-20141111 |access-date=11 November 2014 |work=NBA.com |date=11 November 2014}}</ref>

===Spanish League===
On 14 November 2014, Nedović signed a two-year deal with the Spanish team [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Valencia, Nedovic agree until June of 2016 |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/144840 |access-date=14 November 2014 |work=Euroleague.net |date=14 November 2014}}</ref> Over five [[2014–15 Euroleague|EuroLeague]] games he played for Valencia, he averaged 8 points and 3.6 assists per game. In July 2015, he parted ways with the team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nemanja Nedovic, Valencia Basket part ways |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/166791/nemanja-nedovic-valencia-basket-part-ways.html?ref=crosarka.com |access-date=2 July 2015 |work=sportando.com |date=2 July 2015}}</ref>

On 2 July 2015, the day he parted ways with Valencia, he signed a one-year contract with [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Nedovic, segunda incorporación del Unicaja |url=http://www.unicajabaloncesto.com/noticia-9580-nedovic-segunda-incorporacion-unicaja.html |access-date=2 July 2015 |work=unicajabaloncesto.com |date=2 July 2015 |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150704102405/http://www.unicajabaloncesto.com/noticia-9580-nedovic-segunda-incorporacion-unicaja.html |archive-date=4 July 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 30 May 2016 he signed a new two-year contract with the team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Unicaja Malaga signs Nemanja Nedovic to a two-year contract extension |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/200747/unicaja-malaga-signs-nemanja-nedovic-to-a-two-year-contract-extension.html |access-date=4 October 2016 |work=sportando.com |date=30 May 2016}}</ref> In April 2017, he won the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] with Unicaja after beating [[Valencia Basket|Valencia BC]] in the [[2017 EuroCup Finals|Finals]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/game-center/ |title=7DAYS EuroCup Finals, Game 3: Unicaja Malaga is the champion! |date=5 April 2017 |access-date=6 April 2017 |publisher=Eurocupbasketball.com}}</ref> On 7 June 2017 Nedović re-signed with Unicaja for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Unicaja Malaga announced the extension of Nedovic |url=http://www.eurohoops.net/en/transfers/460610/unicaja-malaga-announced-extension-nedovic/ |access-date=7 June 2017 |work=Eurohoops.net |date=7 June 2017}}</ref> On 27 June 2018 Nedović officially left Unicaja after 3 years.<ref>{{cite news |title=Unicaja Malaga ufficializza l'addio di Nemanja Nedovic |url=https://sportando.basketball/it/spagna/acb/278916/unicaja-malaga-ufficializza-l-addio-di-nemanja-nedovic.html |access-date=27 June 2018 |work=sportando.basketball |date=27 June 2018 |language=it |trans-title=Unicaja Malaga formalizes the departure of Nemanja Nedovic }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Olimpia Milano===
On 27 June 2018 Nedović signed a multi-year deal with the Italian club [[Olimpia Milano]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Milan adds scoring punch with guard Nedovic |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8u4jff7xmn7hd3dy |access-date=27 June 2018 |work=euroleague.net |date=27 June 2018}}</ref>

===Panathinaikos===
On 13 July 2020 Nedović signed with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/nemanja-nedovic-is-a-newcomer-of-panathinaikos/ |title=Nemanja Nedovic is a newcomer of Panathinaikos |date=13 July 2020 |newspaper=Sportando |language=En |access-date=13 July 2020}}</ref> In 10 league games during the 2020-2021 campaign, he averaged 14.8 points, 1.4 rebounds and 2.9 assists, playing around 21 minutes per contest. Additionally, in 25 [[EuroLeague]] games, he averaged 16 points (shooting with 51% from the field, 37% from the 3-point line, and 84% from the free-throw line), 1.9 rebounds and 3.7 assists, playing around 26 minutes per contest.

On 5 July 2021 Nedović officially renewed his contract with the Greek club for another two years. In 26 league games during the 2021-2022 campaign, he averaged 14.4 points, 2.3 rebounds and 2.6 assists, playing around 23 minutes per contest. Additionally, in 26 [[EuroLeague]] games, he averaged 14.3 points (shooting with 53% from the field, 39% from the 3-point line, and 85% from the free-throw line), 2.2 rebounds and 3.2 assists, playing around 24 minutes per contest.

===Return to Crvena zvezda===
On 7 July 2022, Nedović officially returned to [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] after ten years abroad, signing a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nedović zvanično u Zvezdi, ugovor na tri godine |url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/nedovic-zvanicno-u-zvezdi-ugovor-na-tri-godine/424597 |website=mozzartsport.com |access-date=7 July 2022}}</ref>

On 4 June 2025, he agreed to a new two-year contract (with pay cut) with Crvena zvezda.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Petrović |first1=Aleksandar |title=Nedović dogovorio sa Zvezdom na dve godine, uz smanjenje plate |url=https://sportklub.n1info.rs/kosarka/aba-league/nedovic-produzio-ugovor-sa-zvezdom-uz-smanjenje-plate/ |access-date=13 August 2026 |work=n1info.rs |date=4 June 2025 |language=Serbian}}</ref> However, during the summer, he parted ways with the club.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nikolić |first1=Strahinja |title=Nemanja Nedović napustio Crvenu zvezdu - treći bolan odlazak za navijače u nizu |url=https://nova.rs/sport/kosarka/nemanja-nedovic-odlazak-crvena-zvezda-2025-2026/ |access-date=13 August 2026 |work=nova.rs |date=25 August 2025 |language=Serbian}}</ref> For the 2025–2026 season, he was loaned out to [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]], where he helped the team win the [[2025–26 LNB Élite season|2026 French championship]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nemanja Nedović on his future: “I have a contract with Crvena Zvezda, but we’ll know more in the coming weeks”|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1985644/nemanja-nedovic-on-his-future-i-have-a-contract-with-crvena-zvezda-but-well-know-more-in-the-coming-weeks/|website=eurohoops.net|date=June 28, 2026|access-date=July 17, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Nemanja Nedovic.jpg|thumb|Nedović playing for Serbia at [[EuroBasket 2013]]]]
{{see also|2016 Serbia men's Olympic basketball team}}
Nedović was a member of [[Serbia men's national under-20 basketball team|U20 Serbia national basketball team]] in 2009, 2010, and 2011 at [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]]. In 2012, he played with [[Serbia men's national basketball team]] at [[FIBA EuroBasket 2013 qualification]]. During Eurobasket 2013, Nedović's game saw many ups and downs as he led a very young and inexperienced, but nonetheless talented Serbia team, showing great performances against Lithuania and particularly France in a 77–65 blowout, in which he outplayed one of his role models, [[Tony Parker]], scoring 17 points on 5/8 shooting for three. Serbia ended up being swept easily by Spain in the quarterfinals as Nedović and the entire Serbia team struggled offensively.<ref>{{cite web |title=IMPERIOUS SPAIN ROLL PAST SERBIA |url=http://www.eurobasket2013.org/en/cid_8Xfg3jZMG1QuJnp6pnUWd3.gameID_8733-79-A-1.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2013.roundID_8722.teamID_.coid_JwDAaFCnGdkK,SAe1GT2O1.articleMode_on.html |website=eurobasket2013.org |access-date=19 July 2014}}</ref>

He represented Serbia once again at the [[EuroBasket 2015]] under head coach [[Aleksandar Đorđević]], after missing the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=AMBITIOUS SERBIA UNVEIL POWERFUL 12-MAN SQUAD |url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_xUMkR0x,HeIT9w-vv9Ob00.articleMode_on.html |access-date=3 September 2015 |work=eurobasket2015.org |date=2 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905064710/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_xUMkR0x,HeIT9w-vv9Ob00.articleMode_on.html |archive-date=5 September 2015 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> In the first phase of the tournament, Serbia dominated in the toughest [[EuroBasket 2015 Group B|Group B]] with 5–0 record, and then eliminated [[Finland national basketball team|Finland]] and [[Czech Republic national basketball team|Czech Republic]] in the round of 16 and quarterfinal game, respectively. However, they were stopped in the semifinal game by [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania]] with 67–64,<ref>{{cite news |title=LITHUANIA END SERBIAN STREAK, RETURN TO FINAL |url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/gameID_11664-76-A-1.html |access-date=20 September 2015 |work=eurobasket2015.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919004022/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/gameID_11664-76-A-1.html |archive-date=19 September 2015 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> and eventually lost to the host team [[France national basketball team|France]] in the bronze-medal game with 81–68.<ref>{{cite news |title=FRANCE REWARD HOME SUPPORT WITH BRONZE |url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_XCBBt0,vHwcDLI3DN0sTU1.articleMode_on.html |access-date=20 September 2015 |work=eurobasket2015.org |date=20 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150922234352/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_XCBBt0,vHwcDLI3DN0sTU1.articleMode_on.html |archive-date=22 September 2015 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> Over 9 tournament games, Nedović averaged 8.4 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game on 52% shooting from the field.<ref>{{cite web |title=Player profile: Nemanja Nedovic |url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_96799.playerID_62467.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905030106/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_96799.playerID_62467.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=5 September 2015 |website=eurobasket2015.org |publisher=FIBA Europe |access-date=20 September 2015}}</ref>

Nedović also represented Serbia at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]] where they won the silver medal, after losing to the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] in the final game with 96–66.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rio Olympics 2016: USA beat Serbia in men's basketball to win last gold of Games |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/36727948 |access-date=18 September 2017 |work=BBC Sport |date=21 August 2016}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Nedović's strong points are his ball-handling skills and elite athleticism, as he proved to be one of the very best athletes in European basketball. He is known for an excellent first step and can play easily above the rim.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Nemanja-Nedovic-6316/ |title=DraftExpressProfile: Nemanja Nedovic, Stats, Comparisons, and Outlook |access-date=30 August 2013 |archive-date=18 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130818020127/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Nemanja-Nedovic-6316/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was labeled during the [[2013 NBA draft]] as "The European [[Derrick Rose]]" by some [[ESPN]] analysts because of his athleticism, explosiveness, versatility, similar size, and ability to play both guard positions. After he was drafted by the Golden State Warriors, [[Mark Jackson (basketball)|Mark Jackson]], the team coach, has said that Nedović "is a very good athlete with highly deceptive speed."<ref>{{cite news |last=Simmons |first=Rusty |date=13 July 2013 |title=Warriors' top pick Nedovic works with team |work=sfgate.com |url=http://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Warriors-top-pick-Nedovic-works-with-team-4663279.php |access-date=20 October 2013}}</ref>
